findings.finding: SNN held ~5.40m HELG ECCs (7,214,357 now held minus 1,817,032 bought) at fair value through P&L until the 27 Aug block purchase; HELG went from NOK 154.0 (30 Jun) to 176.98 on 27 Aug (deal at 180), so a switch to the equity method at fair value implies a one-off revaluation gain of roughly NOK 124-140m pre-tax (about NOK 0.55-0.6/ECC, ~15% of a normal quarter's EPS) in Q3, the reverse of the -115m H1 drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2026: the HELG revaluation dragged results by 115m (Q2 -60m) and Q1 (miss -4%) moved -2.27%, Q2 (beat +15%) moved +6.31%; the market has not been seen to separate the HELG line from the core.
findings.original_quote: Kursutviklingen på eierskapet i SpareBank 1 Helgeland har også trukket resultat ned med 115 mill. kroner i første halvår 2026. (Q2 report: the price development of the Helgeland stake pulled the result down by NOK 115m in H1 2026.) HELG Q3 report: 'SpareBank 1 Nord-Norge 26,72 %' / '7.214.357'.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the deal and HELG's price are public, but the company never quantified the transition gain, the accounting treatment (fair value as deemed cost vs cost) is inference, and with 4 analysts and no published consensus it is unclear whether estimates carry it. If fully priced, NONG's ~+12% move since 30 Jun would already exceed peers' (SB1NO +20%, MING +16%) -- it does not, so nothing in the tape separates it. Sized small because it is a one-off below operating income.

findings.finding: Peers' Q3 net interest income rose QoQ as the May Norges Bank hike passed through -- SpareBank 1 Sør-Norge +4.2% QoQ to NOK 2,237m, SpareBank 1 Helgeland +16m (+7.8%) to 222m -- consistent with NONG's own Q2 statement that the hike would only reach NII in H2, so NONG's Q3 NII (Q2 970m) likely recovers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII pressure from NIBOR/competition dominated the weak Q1 2026 (-2.27%); Q2 with flat NII still moved +6.31% on other lines.
findings.original_quote: NONG Q2: 'Marginen svekkes som følge av stigende NIBOR i kvartalet, parallelt med at renteøkningen fra Norges Bank ikke materialiseres før andre halvår.' (The margin weakened on rising NIBOR, while the Norges Bank hike does not materialise until H2.)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: NONG itself told the market to expect it, so it sits inside the guided path and is sized small. What may be unpriced is the magnitude HELG's +7.8% QoQ suggests for a northern peer with similar mix.

findings.finding: Moving HELG to proportional consolidation for capital adequacy, with the 26.7% stake carried around NOK 175-180/ECC against HELG book equity of NOK 152.2/ECC, plausibly creates goodwill deducted from CET1 and adds HELG RWA, a likely small negative to NONG's 16.9% CET1 (and to dividend headroom) in the Q3 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction; Norwegian ECC prices are dividend-driven, so CET1 surprises matter at Q4 more than Q3.
findings.why_not_priced: The company stated the treatment but no capital effect; the size is inference. If the market had it, a capital note would have appeared from the four covering brokers -- none found.
